items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: Booker Pitman was the grandson of the late Booker T. WASHINGTON.

ctx.x: They booked us out there and they had no place for us to eat, so we had to eat in the basement of the hotel, We got paid -- we got paid for it, though, we got good money. But, that was back in the days when that was a time of the century that you'd like to forget about.

While in Dallas, Texas, I met a group of young musicians, one was named Bud Johnson, had a brother named Keg Johnson. Budd played tenor sax, Keg played trombone. A -- met an alto player named Booker Pitman. Booker Pitman was the grandson of the late Booker T. WASHINGTON. Booker Pitman I didn't see Booker Pitman for a year or two, until I ran into him out in Springfield, Mass. He was playing with the Blanche Calloway band. Shortly after that Booker Pitman left and went to Europe, he left Europe went to South…

AT one time in ARgentina, they had some kind of big affair and Booker Pitman was in Uruguay, I guess; he was in Montevideo, Uruguay, They came over and got him to lead that parade, He spoke Spanish, he spoke Portuguese, like the natives spoke it. He lived down in South America for 20 some years. I had the pleasure of flying down to Rio de Janeiro and I heard that Booker T. Pitman was playing at the It Club.
